Header:
This sample is from a 55-year-old female who presented with progressive radiating lower back pain. An MRI of the spine was obtained demonstrating two homogeneously enhancing intradural and extramedullary lesions, one at C3 and the other spanning the T12 to L2 spinal levels. Pathologic evaluation revealed a densely cellular glial neoplasm with brisk mitotic activity, microvascular proliferation, perivascular pseudorosettes, and focal necrosis, histologically consistent with ependymoma. Molecular profiling revealed MYCN amplification and variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in PDGFRA (c.1786+7T>C) and APC (c.5399A>G). The overall features were consistent with a diagnosis of Spinal ependymoma, MYCN-amplified, CNS W.H.O. grade 3. 

The patient subsequently experienced intracranial dissemination following standard therapy. HER2 immunostaining was performed on specimen from the patient’s initial operation, motivated by recent systematic profiling of antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) targets in central nervous system tumors [1], showing 2+ to 3+ staining . Multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging confirmed HER2 expression across both quiescent tumor regions and highly proliferative zones. Notably, we found that while HER2 is broadly expressed, EGFR and Ki-67 co-localize to highly proliferative compartments and are inversely correlated with CD44 expression.

[1] Coy et al., Neuro Oncol. 2024 Mar 4;26(3):458-472.

Waypoints.Name: HER2 [low power]
Waypoints.Description: At low power, HER2 showed strong and diffuse expression, with some focal intra-tumoral heterogeneity.

Waypoints.Name: HER2 [high power]
Waypoints.Description: A higher power view demonstrated strong and diffuse membranous HER2 expression, with apparent circumferential expression on tumor cells.

Waypoints.Name: EGFR-positive proliferative nodules
Waypoints.Description: Multiplexed imaging showed that while HER2 was broadly expressed across much of the tumor landscape, EGFR and Ki-67 demonstrated focal expression in discrete tumor nodules, indicating that they exhibited a distinct proliferative phenotype. In contrast, CD44 was enriched in adjacent non-nodular regions, demonstrating an inverse spatial relationship with both EGFR and Ki-67.

Waypoints.Name: Nodule proliferation
Waypoints.Description: There was a strong correlation between EGFR and Ki67 labeling in proliferative areas, and these regions showed low CD44 expression.

Waypoints.Name: Signaling
Waypoints.Description: Examination of intracellular signaling proteins via multiplexed imaging showed distinctive patterning of effectors such as pERK, indicative of focal activation of the MAPK signaling pathway.

Waypoints.Name: Epigenetics
Waypoints.Description: Multiplexed imaging showed patterning of epigenetic markers, with variable levels of H3K27me3, H3K27ac, and H3K4me3 in proliferative EGFR-positive tumor nodules.

Waypoints.Name: Cilia
Waypoints.Description: Upon closer examination, we observed the presence of cilia on ependymoma tumor cells. Staining with gTUB highlighted the basal body, marking the site where the cilium originates, while ARL13b staining clearly visualized the ciliary structures themselves (arrows). Numerous primary and multiciliated cells were observed in proliferative nodules and adjacent CD44-positive regions.

Waypoints.Name: Additional Nodules
Waypoints.Description: Numerous proliferative nodules were observed in this patient sample. A separate region of the tumor was shown, again demonstrating strong expression of EGFR and Ki-67 in nodular regions, with CD44 predominantly expressed in adjacent regions.
